architecture.approach: A client dialog posts a prompt to app/api/generate-event/route.ts. The route lazily builds a Cerebras client from CEREBRAS_API_KEY, requests JSON output, parses the draft, and returns it. The create-event page maps the draft into react-hook-form fields; the normal createEvent mutation remains the only write.

components.name: app/api/generate-event/route.ts
components.description: Validates the prompt, calls Cerebras, and returns the draft or an error.

components.name: app/(main)/create-event/_components/ai-event-creator.tsx
components.description: Dialog, prompt state, request, and success/error toasts.

components.name: app/(main)/create-event/page.tsx
components.description: Maps the generated draft into form fields via handleAIGenerate.

dataModel.flowDescription: The organizer writes a prompt, the client posts it to the route, the route validates it, calls Cerebras with a JSON response format, parses the completion, and returns the five-field draft. The form fills and the organizer still submits the normal validated create-event mutation to persist anything.

securityConsiderations.description: CEREBRAS_API_KEY is read only inside the route handler and is never returned to the client or imported by a client component.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: The dialog disables Generate and shows a spinner while the single provider call runs; manual event creation remains available.

risks.description: The route has no authentication or rate limiting.
risks.mitigation: Require a session and add a per-user limit.
Validate with Zod before applying the draft.

risks.description: The client ignores the HTTP status.
risks.mitigation: Check response.ok and skip onEventGenerated on errors.
